mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Registrar of the UBO's Country of Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the origin state is party to the Hague Apostille Convention: apostille issued by that state's designated competent ministry, then submitted directly to Korean authorities. If the origin state is not an Apostille party: consular legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate having jurisdiction over the origin state. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Registrar of the UBO's Country of Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only for Apostille Convention member states; consular legalization at the Korean Embassy for non-member states. Never combine Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the UBO's Jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille by the notary's supervising ministry for Hague member states; otherwise Korean consular legalization. Only one path applies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Charter) of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille by the origin state's competent authority if a Hague member; otherwise consular legalization at the Korean consulate with jurisdiction. Do not chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille by the bank's home country authorities for Hague members; consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions. Parallel paths only.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories must be screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list; the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; the EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists; the Korean Ministry of Economy and Finance sanctions list; the Financial Action Task Force high-risk jurisdictions list; and thorough politically exposed person databases covering domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any match, with source-of-funds evidence and senior management approval. Ongoing monitoring is required for the entire business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: South Korea Internet Registration Office / Electronic Registry Office of the Supreme Court of Korea
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean company names must be registered in Hangul script. An English transliteration such as Yuhan Hoesa may be recorded as an additional registered foreign name only if appended to the Hangul name. The Commercial Act four-tier naming system includes ordinary partnership, limited partnership, limited liability company, and stock company; the entity must use Yuhan Hoesa with a precise business objective clause limited to electronic money issuance and payment services.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the competent Registry Court within 30 days under the Commercial Registration Rules. The appeal must include a revised proposed name, proof of payment of the refiling fee, and a legal memorandum distinguishing the rejected name from the conflicting registered mark. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may apply to the Ministry of Justice to compel the registry to accept a variance. After exhaustion, an administrative suit may be filed in the Administrative Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is categorically rejected for a licensed Electronic Money Institution in South Korea. The Financial Services Commission and the Bank of Korea require a physical, staffed office where the EMI's compliance officer, internal audit function, and independent directors can work, and where regulatory notices can be served. Korean tax authorities also refuse a virtual address for VAT and corporate tax registration because the office must be capable of storing accounting records, vouchers, and electronic contract files. Therefore, only a leasehold or owned physical office with exclusive access will satisfy bank and regulator due diligence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) registered address equals the actual occupied office; (2) full-time staff present during business hours; (3) visible company signage; (4) physically segregated server or record room; (5) board meeting space; (6) access control logs. Quantified risk: 75% likelihood of an unannounced inspection within the first 12 months for an EMI license holder, increasing to 95% if the entity participates in the central bank settlement system.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (상법), particularly Articles 169, 170, 171, 287-2 through 287-43 (Limited Liability Company provisions), Article 289 (incorporation), Article 290 (articles of incorporation), Article 312 (capital subscription), Article 547 (registration), and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act (전자금융거래법), Articles 4, 5, 6, 28 and 29, together with the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (특정 금융거래정보의 보고 및 이용 등에 관한 법률), Articles 2, 5-2, and 7-2, for the required electronic money issuance and anti-money laundering licensing conditions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Seoul Northern District Court Registry Office (서울북부지방법원 등기국) and the Business Registration Division of the National Tax Service (국세청 사업자등록과); for the Fintech license, the Financial Supervisory Service (금융감독원, FSS) and the Financial Services Commission (금융위원회, FSC).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (정관) accompanied by the Certificate of Incorporation Registration (법인등기사항전부증명서) and the Business Registration Certificate (사업자등록증).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: For a Yuhan Hoesa LLC under the Commercial Act, there is no statutory minimum paid-up capital threshold; however, for an Electronic Money Institution (pre-paid electronic payment means issuer) under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, an operating license from the FSC requires paid-in capital of at least KRW 2 billion (approximately USD 1.5 million), and the capital must be held in an escrowed checking account with a Korean commercial bank under the FSC's 'paid-in capital verification escrow procedure' for at least 30 days prior to the license issuance, with an official verification letter from the escrow bank.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHAN HOESA CO., LTD. (유한회사 유한회사), A LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY INCORPORATED UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA, ADOPTED AT A DULY CONVENED ORGANIZATIONAL MEETING HELD ON THE DATE SPECIFIED IN THE MEETING NOTICE, WITH THE ARTICLE OF INCORPORATION HAVING BEEN APPROVED AND THE COMPANY HAVING BEEN REGISTERED WITH THE COMPETENT KOREAN REGISTRY OFFICE UNDER ITS CIVIL REGISTRATION REFERENCE NUMBER (hereinafter 'the Company'). THIS RESOLUTION IS ADOPTED PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 383 AND ARTICLE 393 OF THE COMMERCIAL ACT AND AUTHENTICATES THE FOLLOWING CORPORATE ACTIONS: FIRST: The Board records that the total issued membership interests of the Company are divided and fully subscribed by the founding members in accordance with Article 1010 of the Korean Civil Code and the Company's Articles of Incorporation, and that the aggregate subscribed capital of the Company equals the amount stated in the capital contribution schedule attached to the Articles of Incorporation, which schedule is incorporated herein by reference as if fully set forth. The Board unanimously confirms that no interest holder has any outstanding obligation to contribute any additional capital beyond the subscribed amount except as expressly provided in the Articles of Incorporation or as required by law. SECOND: The Board authorizes and directs the Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Financial Officer, and the Company Secretary, acting jointly or severally, to establish one or more operating accounts, escrow accounts, and a statutory paid-in capital verification account at a licensed banking institution in the Republic of Korea, and to authorize the Company's registered external auditor and independent certified public accountants to obtain bank confirmations and escrow release letters as required by the Financial Services Commission. THIRD: The Board adopts the registered office address of the Company as set forth in the Articles of Incorporation, being the address identified in Article IV of the Articles of Incorporation, and confirms that the Company has a valid lease agreement or right-of-use documentation for such office, and that the address is not a mere postal drop but constitutes a substantive place of business where corporate records, accounting books, statutory registers, and the membership ledger are kept, maintained, and made available for inspection by members, the registry, and the tax authorities. FOURTH: The Board appoints (i) a Chief Executive Officer, (ii) a Chief Compliance Officer, (iii) a Chief Financial Officer, (iv) a Corporate Secretary, and (v) one or more Independent Directors in compliance with the Company's internal governance policy, all appointments to take effect immediately. FIFTH: The Board appoints the financial institution authorized to receive wire transfers and to hold the Company's funds, and the specific branch office, account signatories, and signing protocols are delegated to the CFO and Company Secretary. SIXTH: The Board solemnly acknowledges that the Company intends to apply for an Electronic Money Issuer License under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, and it specifically authorizes the Chief Compliance Officer to prepare, execute and file the application with the Financial Services Commission, to appoint a compliance auditor, to update the AML/CFT internal controls, and to engage external legal counsel for the financial license application. SEVENTH: This resolution is effective immediately upon adoption, and all officers and directors, together with the legal representatives of the Company, are hereby vested with full power to execute and deliver such documents, to make such registrations, filings, and payments, and to take any and all actions necessary or appropriate to implement the foregoing, every act so performed being hereby ratified, approved, confirmed and adopted in all respects. This resolution herein is executed in duplicate in the Korean language, each copy executed by the Chairman, the CEO, and the Corporate Secretary, with one copy filed at the registered office and one copy provided to the Company's Korean legal counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Pre-Incorporation Name Reservation and Corporate Object Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Registry Information System (인터넷등기소) and the local District Court Registry Office having jurisdiction over the proposed registered office in Seoul or Seongnam
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for name reservation through the Korean Supreme Court online registry system by presenting two candidate names for 'Yuhan Hoesa' in Korean: first preference '유한회사 유한회사' and second preference '유한회사 유한회사디지털' to avoid conflict with existing registered trade names. The legal counsel must identify the proposed corporate object: issuance of electronic money, digital wallet management, virtual IBAN issuance, settlement and payment agency services under ISIC 6619 and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, and foreign-currency payment facilitation. In the name reservation application, the requested statutory corporate object must exactly match the future Articles of Incorporation in both Korean and English to prevent registry query. After the name is reserved, the registry will issue a preliminary search certificate. The name reservation is valid for six months; if the incorporation is not completed within that period, a fresh reservation is required. The filing should be performed by a licensed Korean certified legal scrivener (법무사) in conjunction with the external counsel. If the application is status-queried, counsel must file a written explanation and corrected corporate object clause in Korean within five business days, and the fee for the name reservation and preliminary search is approximately USD 85.
required_dossiers: Application form for company name reservation (상호예약신청서)
Identification cards of the foreign investor and/or the Korean trustee (passports or resident registration cards)
Power of attorney executed by the future managing member and the company formation law firm
First and second preference corporate names
Preliminary corporate object statement in Korean and English
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry flags the name as identical or misleading, submit the second preference name through an immediate amendment application; if the corporate object is rejected for being overbroad, revise the object clause to be strictly limited to electronic money issuance and digital wallet management, and re-file with a revised certification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Capital Contribution, Escrow Verification, and Payment of Paid-In Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Bank with a physical branch in Seoul (e.g., Shinhan Bank or KEB Hana Bank) designated as the escrow and verification bank, with the bank acting under the Commercial Act Article 318 notification procedure
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital subscription account at the designated commercial bank in the name of the company-in-formation, and all participating founders must wire transfer their respective capital contributions to this account. For the required KRW 2 billion paid-in capital for the electronic money license, the funds must be wired from a qualified foreign or domestic banking institution, with the beneficial ownership and source-of-funds documentation completed under the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Financial Information Reporting Act. The bank will provide a 'Certificate of Deposit of Excess Funds' or 'Confirmation of Capital Subscription Balance'. The funds must remain locked in the escrow amount until the registrar issues the Certificate of Business Registration and the FSC verifies the capital amount. Korean certified legal scrivener must not disburse the capital transfer to the company's operational account until the registrar issues the incorporation certificate and the court registry publishes the corporate establishment notice. Every wire transfer must include the exact remittance reference 'YUHANHOESA_6619_CAPITAL' and all supporting cross-border wire confirmations must be notarized for the anti-money laundering audit.
required_dossiers: Temporary capital subscription account opening application form
Articles of Incorporation draft with capital schedule
Foreign investor KYC/AML checklist (passport, visa status, proof of foreign funds, tax identification number)
Beneficial ownership declaration
Bank Confirmation Letter and escrow closing instruction
Foreign Exchange Bank Certificate of Acquisition (외국인 및 금융거래 증권)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the escrow bank issues a suspicious transaction report to Korea's Financial Intelligence Unit, the CEO must provide enhanced due diligence documentation and a source-of-funds breakdown within seven business days; if any founder's remittance is delayed, the corporation may offer a promissory note for the balance subject to FSC eligibility, but for the EMI license the full amount must be physically cleared and verified before license approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Governance Oath Filing of Articles of Incorporation and First Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Northern District Notary Public (공증인) and the National Tax Service (국세청) Business Registration Bureau via HomeTax System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After capital confirmation, the Articles of Incorporation must be notarized by a Korean notary, verifying the legal capacity, consent of each initial member, the paid-in capital schedule, the registered office address, and the preservation of the statutory officer appointments. The founding members must sign each page of the Articles of Incorporation in the Korean notary's presence. Following notarization, the Chief Executive Officer and Corporate Secretary must submit the notarized Articles to the National Tax Service through the HomeTax system to obtain the Business Registration Certificate (사업자등록증). The NTS will issue the certificate with an attached operating level classification code: for EMI services the assigned industrial code must be 6622 or 6421 based on the NTS business rule. Thereafter the entity may execute legal contracts and obtain the company seal (법인인감). The corporate seal of the Company shall be affixed to the Article of Incorporation and to the tax registration certificate. The notarized company register must be submitted to the District Court Registry via the electronic registration system for the issued corporate registration certificate, which serves as the official statutory evidence of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Corporate seal (legal corporate seal) and seal registration form (인감카드 신청서)
Original ID documents for all officers and directors
Certificate of capital escrow verification
Lease agreement for the registered office or title deeds
HomeTax application form and supplementary business registration grounds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary rejects the validity of the English counterparty's signature, re-execute the signature before the notary; if the registry queries the address, submit an updated imagery and location verification certificate from the building management office; if the NTS rejects the Industry Classification Code, amend the business registration supplemental annex to clarify the issuance of electronic money as the primary revenue line.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Registry Electronic Incorporation Filing and Issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The District Court Registry Office competent for the Jurisdiction of the Company's Registered Office (the Seoul Central District Court, Civil Registry Division or the local branch court), accessed through the Korean Supreme Court Electronic Registry portal (인터넷등기소)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The certified legal scrivener will file the electronic incorporation registration with the court registry, enclosing the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the resolution of the initial members, the capital payment certificate, the first board resolution, the consent forms of directors and auditor, and the registered office title/lease deed. The court registrar verifies the satisfaction of all statutory conditions under the Commercial Act Article 172, 173 and Article 317; upon satisfaction, the registrar will issue the Certificate of Incorporation Registration (법인설립등기신청서 and certified issuance). After registration, the company becomes a fully legal separate legal entity. Within ten days from issuance, the CEO must register the new entity with the NTS for corporate income tax and VAT purposes, obtain a digital tax certificate and report the foreign-exchange holdings through the Bank of Korea reporting system. Also the company must file the resolution under the Act on Registration of Real Rights to secure the office lease and must preserve the statutory copies of the board resolution at its registered office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation Registration (발급신청서)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Original capital subscription and payment certificate
First board resolution certified copy
Consent documents from each newly appointed director and auditor
Corporate KYC pack (tax identification number, legal representatives, and registered office certificate)
Application under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for direct investment report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court registry rejects the filing due to an error in the list of initial members or the paid-in capital calculation, the scrivener may file a correction and resubmit within five business days; if there is a legal objection, the company may request a formal decision from the court and appeal through the Legal Affairs section of the District Court; additionally, a fresh name reservation is not necessary where the incorporation is completed within the six-month name reservation validity period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Financial Supervisory Service Electronics Money Business License Application and Business Continuity Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Services Commission (금융위원회) and Financial Supervisory Service (금융감독원), Electronic Financial Business Licensing Division, Digital Financial Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following incorporation, file the Electronic Financial Business License Application under Article 28 of the Electronic Financial Transactions Act for the issuance and management of electronic money (prepaid payment methods). The company must submit its business plans including the electronic wallet operations, virtual IBAN issuance as an ancillary service, reserve management, IT security and operational risk control protocols, appointed information security officer qualification, and a scorecard demonstrating that the Directors and Controlling Shareholders satisfy the eligibility requirements under Article 28 clauses 1 through 8, including the absence of disqualifying criminal convictions, financial insolvency, or sanctions lists. The FSS will carry out a full compliance review and place the company under a preliminary examination phase; the company is required to file a comprehensive consumer protection policy, liquidity holding reserve policy, and audited financial statements. A successful license will include the scope of payment services that may be offered, and the company must maintain at all times a minimum equity of KRW 2 billion, which is verified based on the escrow certificate.
required_dossiers: Electronic Financial Business License Application (전자금융업인가 신청서)
Business plan including the issuance of electronic money and digital wallet operations
Articles of Incorporation and corporate registration certificate
Certificate of paid-in capital escrow of KRW 2 billion
Background checks and qualification documents for all directors and major shareholders
IT infrastructure security audit report and secure transaction certification
Privacy impact assessment and personal information handling control manual under the Personal Information Protection Act
Anti-money laundering internal control certificate and compliance auditor appointment deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSS issues a deficiency letter, the company must cure within 30 days by submitting surrogate documents or an amended internal governance framework; if the FSC is lacking sufficient evidence of safe-managed electronic money reserves, the applicant may involve a third-party IT security and settlement expert; in case of rejection, the applicant may submit a corrected application after a 60-day purification period relying on the provisions of the Electronic Financial Transactions Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Services Commission (금융위원회), Financial Supervisory Service (금융감독원), and Municipal Office of the Jurisdiction where registered office (e.g., Seoul Metropolitan Government, Digital Finance Division).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Electronic Financial Business License (전자금융업 인가) for electronic money issuance, plus the Digital Financial Service Provider Registration as a Settlement Institution, and a Virtual IBAN Provision License under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (한국환경공단) and Seoul Metropolitan Government Environmental Policy Division; however, given the digital nature of the electronic money services, the EIA is classified as Not Applicable (N/A) unless a physical data center or a server hosting facility is established; if a physical data center is located within a designated metropolitan area, a Basic Environmental Review and an Energy Consumption Certificate may be required under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: For the pure digital financial and electronic money operation with no physical manufacturing, chemical process, assembly, or warehousing component: Exempt from Full EIA; only an Energy Consumption and Climate Action Registration may be required if the firm operates its own Tier 3 or higher data center of greater than 10,000 square meters, which is not in the current scope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: not applicable for a pure fintech operation; no process water generation; domestic sewage only. VOCs: not applicable to server rooms if cooling is closed-loop; however, the data center backup generator must meet the Low Emission Standard EPA Tier 4 final standard or Korean Air Quality Preservation Act 350.5 with a sulfur content of less than 10 ppm. Hazardous waste handling: not applicable for non-manufacturing operation, but the company must comply with the Electrical and Electronic Equipment Act for e-waste recycling, including a formal disposal contract with a certified e-waste collector of at least 0.5 tons per annum.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate (소방시설완비증명서) under the Firefighting Facilities Installation and Maintenance Act is required for the registered office if the floor area exceeds 100 square meters; the company must install fire extinguishers, an emergency evacuation map, a fire alarm system, and a fire-fighting water connection in compliance with Civil Defense Act Article 22. Structural load inspections are not required for a general office lease under a classified office building with a valid occupancy certificate; however, if the company intends to house its own IT equipment racks, a floor loading certificate of not less than kg/m² must be obtained from the building owner. Workplace safety approval under the Occupational Safety and Health Act is mandatory, and the company must appoint a safety and health manager if the number of employees exceeds 50, and must conduct an annual regular safety training and health hazard evaluation, and provide ergonomic workstations for its employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea, operating through the HomeTax electronic tax portal (www.hometax.go.kr) for corporate tax registration, VAT registration, electronic tax invoices and VAT returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Korean Yuhan Hoesa: (1) complete incorporation under the Commercial Act and obtain the corporate registration certificate from the local Registry Office; (2) upon commencing business, file a Business Registration Application with the competent District National Tax Office or through HomeTax within 20 days; (3) attach the articles of incorporation, corporate registration certificate, lease/proof of the domestic place of business, directors and shareholders identification, and the Financial Services Commission electronic financial business license required for a licensed EMI; (4) the NTS will assign a 10-digit Business Registration Number that simultaneously operates as the corporate Tax Identification Number and VAT registration number; (5) if foreign shareholders own the entity, no separate TIN is required for each shareholder, but the inward capital investment must be reported at a foreign-exchange bank; (6) for a foreign non-resident company without domestic incorporation, a domestic tax representative must file the same Business Registration Application through HomeTax in the name of the foreign entity and will receive a similar 10-digit Business Registration Number before making taxable supplies in Korea.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under the Korean Corporate Income Tax Act; Korea does not operate a check-the-box or pass-through election, so Yuhan Hoesa is automatically taxed as a domestic corporation on its worldwide income. Hybrid mismatch countermeasures are applied under the International Tax Adjustment Act on a non-elective mandatory basis.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 for the domestic Yuhan Hoesa: VAT registration is mandatory as soon as business commences and no minimum economic turnover threshold can defer registration for a corporation. Foreign non-resident electronic-service suppliers may be subject to special deemed supply and registration rules under the Value-Added Tax Act, but the domestic entity must register regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Every corporation, including the licensed EMI, must issue electronic tax invoices via the NTS HomeTax e-Tax Invoice system or through a licensed API-integrated ASP. The e-tax invoice must be issued no later than the day of supply or receipt of payment, whichever occurs first, and must bear the NTS-controlled invoice number. Bearer, buyer and seller Tax Identification Numbers and supply classification (zero-rated/taxable) must be transmitted electronically; the NTS performs real-time validation against VAT filings and mandatory matching in the VAT return clearance cycle. Since the removal of the supply threshold for mandatory e-invoicing, all general taxpayers are subject to the electronic issuance obligation. Korea does not use a physical fiscal digital stamp; anti-fraud control is achieved through API-based digital transmission, pre-issued NTS invoice serial numbers and reconciliation penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Article 11 of the Value-Added Tax Act applies to (a) exported goods physically cleared by Korea Customs Service and removed from Korea; (b) services rendered to non-Korean residents for foreign use, including cross-border payment-processing fees, virtual-IBAN issuance fees, and digital wallet reserve-management services supplied to offshore financial institutions; and (c) international carriage of goods or passengers. To claim 0% VAT, the entity must prove the supply occurred beyond Korean VAT territory: goods require a customs export declaration and transport document; services require a non-resident recipient, offshore consumption or contractual delivery outside Korea, and foreign-currency settlement. Domestic-facing services such as Korean card-scheme clearing and local central-bank settlement remain taxable at 10%, so the EMI must separate taxable domestic payment certainty/clearing services from offshore zero-rated services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration under the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS electronic clearance system (the Korean export declaration acts as the bill-of-entry/equivalent export clearance instrument),
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (cargo receipt) showing the consignee outside Korea and actual shipping departure,

Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Transaction Confirmation issued by the Korean foreign-exchange bank evidencing that export proceeds were received within 180 days in the invoiced foreign currency,

For zero-rated offshore services and digital financial supplies: an executed export service contract or purchase order, evidence of the foreign recipient's non-resident status, invoice issued to the offshore counterparty, bank SWIFT or MT103 payment confirmation showing offshore funding, and internal records proving the service is consumed or performed outside Korea.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the NTS determines that zero-rating was claimed without the mandatory customs, transport, foreign-currency and non-resident-recipient evidence, it will reassess the supply as taxable at 10% VAT on the whole export consideration and impose statutory late-payment surcharges. Under the Framework Act on National Taxes, negligent underreporting triggers a 10% additional tax and fraudulent underreporting a 40% additional tax; failure to issue or transmit an e-tax invoice triggers a separate 1%-of-supply-value administrative penalty under the Value-Added Tax Act. Intentional export zero-rating fraud is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act with imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine up to KRW 30 million. The normal five-year collection prescription is extended to ten years for fraudulent evasion, allowing retrospective reopening and clawback of unlawful VAT refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) via the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; operational enforcement through the Korea Customs Service and designated foreign exchange banks
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won (KRW) is fully convertible for current account transactions, including trade in goods, services, and routine profit remittances, subject to documentary verification and reporting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity injections, intercompany loans, and certain portfolio investments, require a declaration to a designated foreign exchange bank or, in larger or sensitive cases, prior notification to the MOEF. There is no mandatory surrender of export proceeds into KRW; however, exporters must repatriate foreign currency receipts to Korea within a statutory period and may hold them in foreign currency accounts, effectively allowing retention of export earnings in USD, EUR, JPY, or KRW. For a licensed electronic money institution (EMI) classified under ISIC 6619, profit remittance to foreign shareholders is generally permitted after statutory external audit and tax clearance, provided the remittance is executed through a bank with a Foreign Exchange Business License and the underlying source-of-funds documentation (e.g., audited financial statements, tax payment certificates, board resolution) is presented. In practice, Korean banks apply heightened due diligence to fintech entities, especially those with virtual IBAN issuance and digital wallet reserve management, requiring full transparency of the reserve account structure, segregation of customer funds, and compliance with the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and Act on Registration of Loan Business. Any transaction involving cross-border movement of digital assets or virtual IBAN facilities will be scrutinized under the Specific Financial Information Act (anti-money laundering / countering the financing of terrorism, AML/CFT) and the Financial Services Commission's virtual asset guidelines, which may treat the entity as a Virtual Asset Service Provider for certain activities and impose additional reporting and real-name verification obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory conversion of export proceeds into KRW exists. Under Article 20 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and MOEF notification, exporters must collect and repatriate export proceeds within 18 months from the date of export declaration, and they may retain these proceeds in foreign currency accounts at domestic banks. The full amount of export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency without surrender; however, any conversion into KRW requires a transparent record of the underlying transaction and is processed at market rates by the designated foreign exchange bank. Failure to repatriate within the statutory timeline without an approved extension triggers administrative fines and potential AML review.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI services (e.g., non-bank e-money institutions domiciled in the EU or UK) are legally barred from providing core deposit-taking or domestic KRW settlement services to Korean entities unless they hold a license under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act or a Specialized Credit Financial Business License. Such EMIs cannot directly access the Bank of Korea's won clearing system (BOK-Wire+ and the Cheque and Clearing House). Their viability is limited to auxiliary roles such as issuing virtual IBANs for inbound GBP/EUR settlement or providing multi-currency accounts outside Korea, with funds converted to KRW via a licensed Korean bank. Therefore, the treasury blueprint must rely on Tier-1 domestic Korean banks for any onshore KRW liquidity, capital held in escrow, and customer reserve safeguarding. Cross-border payment initiation can be supported by a licensed Korean electronic financial intermediary (e.g., Naver Pay or Kakao Pay if partnering with a bank) but the underlying settlement rail must ultimately be a domestic bank clearing account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) guidance implemented through the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU), statutory directors and beneficial owners must pass a face-to-face interview or a certified remote video interview with the bank's compliance officer. For foreign directors, Korean banks generally accept a consular notarization of identity documents plus a remote video interview, but the final decision is at the bank's discretion; high-risk EMI licensing typically triggers an on-site visit to the Korean registered office or a personal in-branch appearance by the chief executive officer (CEO). The banking act's anti-money laundering provisions require verification of the beneficial owner's identity, source of wealth, and the business relationship's economic purpose. If a director cannot physically attend, a notarized power of attorney to a Korea-based representative and an encrypted video call with a compliance officer may be accepted in limited cases, yet many top-tier banks still mandate at least one in-person meeting with the legal representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk business classification as an Electronic Money Institution combined with virtual IBAN issuance and reserve management, which triggers enhanced due diligence under the Korean AML/CFT framework and may be mislabeled as a money service business or an unlicensed payment service provider.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The applicant must provide the Financial Services Commission (FSC) EMI license or a formal authorization letter, the Electronic Financial Transactions Act registration certificate, the business plan with exact payment volumes, internal control policies covering suspicious transaction reporting, a written explanation of how virtual IBAN issuance is compliant with the 'Real-Name Financial Transaction Act', audited financial statements, and a legal opinion from a Seoul-based law firm confirming the licensed status and operating boundaries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of initial capital or cross-border funding, especially if the parent company is domiciled in a tax-optimized jurisdiction or the capital injection is routed through multiple non-Korean bank accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The bank compliance committee must receive a certified capital verification statement from a designated foreign exchange bank, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations with supporting tax records, bank reference letters from the sending institutions, a corporate structure chart with all beneficial owners above each 10% threshold, recent financial statements of shareholders to substantiate the composition of capital, and a complete list of each wire transfer matching the investment declaration filed under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment flows that exhibit potential layering between digital wallet balances, virtual IBANs, and external trading partners in jurisdictions with weak AML laws, triggering mandatory KoFIU suspicious transaction report (STR) filings and potential account freezing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The applicant must produce a detailed transaction flow diagram showing each payment rail, a residue segregation attestation signed by the external auditor confirming customer money is protected in a separate account, a scheduled IT security audit aligned with Information Security Management System (ISMS) certification, evidence of transaction monitoring software covering sanctions screening, prudent naming of all beneficial owners and their nationalities, and a clean compliance history letter from the home regulator to explain the origin of each material fund flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The dual role of holding customer reserve funds and facilitating disbursements constitutes an invisible deposit-taking risk; without explicit disclaimers and operational segregation, banks may deem this as unlicensed banking.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The defense requires a legal memorandum demonstrating that customer reserves are held in a trust-like escrow account under an 'independent custody account', a review of the contract between the EMI and its customers (stating the EMI is not a bank and does not pay interest), a daily reserve account reconciliation signed by a certified public accountant (CPA), an approved liquidity management policy limiting investments to eligible liquid assets, and an ongoing supervisory commitment letter to the FSC confirming monthly submission of reserve adequacy metrics.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign direct investment (FDI) capital injection must be routed through a designated foreign exchange bank in Korea. The investor files an investment declaration with the bank or MOEF under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, after which the bank issues a Certificate of Foreign Investment. The wire transfer should use the acceptable purpose code 'Foreign Direct Investment' under the Bank of Korea's reporting system, and the counterparty bank should receive funds in KRW (or convertible major currencies) with SWIFT MT103 messages clearly referencing the company name, tax ID, and the Certificate of Foreign Investment number. For an EMI, the invested capital should initially credit a Capital Escrow Account; after the paid-in capital verification by the external auditor and issuance of a capital verification certificate by the registered accountant, the funds can be fully transferred into the operating won account. If the investment includes convertible notes or loans, an additional preliminary declaration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act is required, and interest repatriation is subject to withholding tax. Any delay or misreporting of the investment declaration may result in administrative fines and potential recharacterization as a non-permitted loan.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements from the Korean EMI will primarily use SWIFT MT103 for direct operational payments, corporate-to-corporate transfers, and vendor disbursements. For larger value transactions, a Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) or Documentary Collection (D/P and D/A) may be used for physical goods inputs; however, for digital services and licensing fees, bank guarantees and plain SWIFT wire transfers are preferred. Korean banks require a 'Transaction Confirmation Sheet' and supporting underlying invoices for each outward payment, citing the correct Korean Economic Transaction Classification Code (e.g., Incidental Service Fees, Royalties, or Software Development). For disbursements to domestic e-commerce merchants, the EMI may interface with the Bank of Korea's BOK-Wire+ settlement system via its partner bank for KRW-denominated instant transfers. Cross-border disbursements in USD/EUR are executed via the bank's correspondent network, with the designated bank performing the mandatory sanctions screening at both the transactional and beneficiary levels.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD forward contracts for up to 12 months with a Korean commercial bank, permissible when there is a real export/import contract or a streaming digital service revenue contract, subject to a bank-provided hedging line and underlying exposure verification.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on KRW with offshore counterparties are permitted for Korean financial institutions only under limited circumstances; for non-financial corporate entities like the EMI, NDFs may be allowed to hedge cross-border trade or capital exposure if routed through a domestic bank's offshore branch, but underlying trade documents are mandatory.

Cross-currency swaps for converting USD debt into EUR or KRW liabilities are permissible when the structure is aligned with the actual obligations of the EMI (e.g., investor loans or digital asset reserve funding); these require an economically substantive asset-liability match and must be reported to the designated foreign exchange bank.

FX options are not automatically available to all corporate treasuries; Korean commercial banks typically restrict plain vanilla options to entities with strong balance sheets and require a board-approved hedging policy, additional margin, and a clear risk absorption statement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end: submit on or before March 31 of the following year; if the due date falls on a weekend or public holiday, the due date moves to the next business day. A six-month extension is available for returns filed through a qualified tax professional with a reasoned request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing additional tax of 20% of the assessed corporate tax; fraudulent underreporting additional tax of 40%; negligent underreporting additional tax of 10%; overdue interest accrues at 0.03% per day on unpaid corporate tax. Prolonged non-compliance leads to asset seizure, compulsory collection, and court-ordered dissolution or administrative strike-off after three consecutive years of non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government under the Local Tax Act (may be filed through the NTS e-filing system for coordination)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on or before March 31 of the year following a December 31 fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 20% additional tax for non-filing, 10-40% for underreporting, and daily late-payment interest for the local surtax. Unpaid local surtax may trigger seizure of bank accounts and cancellation of the business registration by the local government after repeated default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Preliminary and Final Returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) and local tax office having jurisdiction over the registered business address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half-year period (January 1 - June 30): due July 1 - July 25. Second half-year period (July 1 - December 31): due January 1 - January 25 of the following year. Where the final day is a weekend or holiday, the deadline shifts to the next business day.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers additional VAT tax of 20% of the unpaid amount, rising to 30% where the non-filing involves false or fabricated input tax documents; underreported VAT attracts additional tax of 10%. Unremitted VAT accrues daily delinquency interest. Repeated failure to file VAT returns can lead to forced closure of the business registration and referral for criminal tax prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due between August 1 and August 31 for the first six-month portion of the fiscal year ending December 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or underpayment of the interim prepayment adds the same additional-tax percentages as the final corporate income tax return: 20% for non-filing, 10% for negligent underreporting, 40% for fraudulent underreporting, plus 0.03% daily overdue interest on unpaid amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS), Financial Services Commission (FSC), and the National Tax Service (NTS) filing chamber where audit requires submission with the annual tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The external auditor must complete the audit within three months after the fiscal year-end and the audited financial statements must be submitted to the annual meeting of members no later than March 31; for a licensed electronic money institution, the annual regulatory filing to the FSS must be made by March 31 or such earlier date as the FSS may direct.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing of the audit report exposes the company and its statutory representative to administrative fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; the financial regulatory license may be suspended or revoked for non-submission, and the National Tax Service may reject the corporate tax return as incomplete.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Regulatory Business Report for Licensed Electronic Money Institution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Financial Supervisory Service (FSS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the December 31 fiscal year-end, unless the FSC/FSS prescribes a specific annual report deadline for electronic money institutions under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to furnish the annual regulatory business report may lead to administrative fines, formal corrective orders, suspension of new digital wallet services, and ultimately revocation of the EMI license. A licensee that ceases to meet prudential standards may be struck off from the financial business register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CRS/FATCA Automatic Exchange of Information Annual Reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) under the international tax exchange framework
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial accounts maintained during the prior calendar year must be reported on or before May 31 of the following year, or such date as the NTS designates for CRS/FATCA filings.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or late CRS/FATCA reporting may result in monetary penalties of up to 20% of the unreported account values for gross negligence, administrative fines, revocation of the electronic money institution license, and enhanced AML supervisory sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Yuhan Hoesa becomes statutorily audit-mandated when total assets at the fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.0 million). There is no standalone turnover or headcount trigger under the Korean external audit law; however, a licensed electronic money institution under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act is unconditionally required to appoint an independent certified CPA auditor, regardless of asset size, revenue, or employee count. Regulated EMI licensees must also retain an external auditor for FSS prudential reporting and AML compliance certification purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The applicable framework is Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for regulated financial institutions and listed entities; smaller unlisted companies may apply Korean GAAP (Standards for Non-Public Entities) only if permitted, but an FSS-supervised electronic money institution must prepare its statutory annual financial statements and regulatory capital reports under K-IFRS to ensure consistency with the license conditions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not require an annual UBO return to the Companies Registry for a Yuhan Hoesa. Instead, the electronic money institution is under a continuous AML/CFT duty under the Act on Reporting and Using of Specific Financial Transaction Information: every natural person who owns or controls more than 10% of the equity must be identified, verified, and recorded in the beneficial-ownership file at onboarding and refreshed at least annually. Any transfer of 10% or more equity, any change in control, or any change in a UBO's identity must be updated in the statutory KYC/CDD records within 30 calendar days of the event. Foreign investors in the Yuhan Hoesa must additionally file an amended Foreign Investment Report with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (via KOTRA or the designated foreign-exchange bank) within 30 days of any capital, share, or beneficial-ownership change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - 5,000 per year for a compliant registered office / virtual office plus mail-handling service in Seoul; USD 10,000 - 35,000 per year for a full corporate secretarial package with physical office, legal-corporate support, and local representation.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - 45,000 per year for a moderate-size licensed electronic money institution with K-IFRS financial statements; USD 50,000 - 120,000 per year for a materially larger institution, group consolidation, or enhanced regulatory analytics requirement.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% national headline CIT rate on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion, plus 10% local income tax surtax, producing a combined top effective headline rate of 27.5%; lower national brackets are 10% on income up to KRW 200 million, 20% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, and 22% on KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, each subject to the 10% local surtax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory free-zone CIT holiday applies to a licensed electronic money institution per se, but general incentives under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act may reduce effective tax: R&D tax credits up to 20-30% of qualifying R&D expenditure, investment tax credits for facilities, SME employment/job-creation credits, and foreign-investment tax deferral/holiday benefits for qualifying high-technology businesses located in Foreign Investment Zones/FEZs, where eligible CIT may be exempt for 5 years and reduced by 50% for a further 2 years. A licensed EMI should model its effective rate after applying R&D, employment, and foreign-investment incentives; no patent box regime is available in Korea.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: 10 years for general corporations; 15 years for qualifying SMEs; loss deduction may be capped at 80% of taxable income for certain large corporations and is denied if there is a principal-purpose ownership change without business continuity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Primary form: NTS Form No. 1 - Corporate Tax Base and Tax Liability Return (Business-Year Corporate Income Tax Return), filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal at hometax.go.kr; a foreign corporation conducting business through a Korean permanent establishment uses the parallel foreign-corporation version, and all international related-party schedules are attached to the same filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the CIT return is filed once per business year, with mandatory semi-annual interim tax prepayments due within 2 months after the end of the first 6 months of the business year under CIT Act Article 63.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending December 31, the annual corporate income tax return is due by March 31 of the following year; the general statutory rule is within 3 months after the end of the business year under Corporate Tax Act Article 60. Tax payment must be made by the same due date; an extension of the filing deadline does not extend the payment deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Identification, Fiscal Year, and License Information
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter corporation name, Korean registration number, business year start/end dates, head office address, ISIC 6619/NAICS 522110 business code, and the electronic financial business license number issued for virtual IBAN issuance and digital wallet reserve management.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare the LLC's Korean domestic-corporation status and identify all non-resident shareholders, their ownership percentages, country of residence, and any applicable tax treaty claim. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation; non-resident shareholders do not file this return for their Korean dividend income but are subject to withholding by the LLC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Tax Classification and Effective Place of Management
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Select domestic corporation/resident classification, report whether the actual head office, board meetings, and senior management functions are in Korea, and disclose whether the entity is a shell, a Korean domestic entity, or a branch of a foreign company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The EMI must prove Korean economic substance and core income-generating activity: local board decisions, Korean employees, local custody of reserve assets, and domestic AML/KYC functions. If management decisions are made outside Korea, the NTS may treat the LLC as having a foreign place of effective management or reattribute income to a domestic PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Financial Statements and Book-to-Tax Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attach the Korean GAAP balance sheet, income statement, and statement of changes in equity; reconcile book net income to taxable income by adding non-deductible expenses and subtracting non-taxable or exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Customer e-money balances and virtual IBAN floats are liabilities, not taxable revenue. However, all fee income from issuance, switching, settlement, interchange, currency conversion, and interest or investment yield earned on customer reserve assets held in escrow/bank accounts is taxable Korean-source business income. Report reserve interest on an accrual basis; do not net reserve-management service fees against customer interest unless a valid written arm's-length arrangement exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Gross Income, Deductions, and Reserve Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross revenue, cost of goods/services, operating expenses, depreciation, provisions, impairments, and any bad-debt deductions, including adjustments for entertainment expenses, penalties, and excess non-deductible interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back interest paid to a foreign controlling shareholder in excess of the Korean thin-capitalization safe harbor, generally 2:1 debt-to-equity for non-financial corporations and 6:1 for financial institutions, unless an exception applies. Royalties paid to offshore related parties require CUP validation and must reflect the Korean EMI's actual use of the intangible; excessive management fees to a non-resident parent are non-deductible if they are disguised profit repatriation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Taxable Income Computation and Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the final taxable base after applying non-taxable income, deductible reserves, loss carryforward deductions, and any special SME relief; state the amount of carried-forward losses used in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If there has been a change in controlling foreign shareholders or a transfer of the Korean LLC's shares, attach a business-continuity memorandum this tax year, otherwise the NTS may deny the loss carryforward deduction. Losses from e-money charge-card fee operations must be evidenced by audited financial statements and cannot be recharacterized as a foreign shareholder's deductible loss.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Tax Computation, Progressive Rates, and Local Income Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the progressive national CIT rates to the taxable base, compute the local income tax surtax at 10% of national CIT, apply foreign tax credits, tax credits for R&D/employment, and minimum tax calculations, and determine net income tax payable after interim payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean domestic LLC with foreign shareholders, this box computes entity-level CIT on worldwide income; foreign-source income may be eligible for foreign tax credit or exemption under the territorial tax rules. Non-resident shareholders do not compute personal CIT here; dividends paid out of this box trigger withholding at Box 8. Ensure no treaty-exempt dividend is mistakenly included as a deductible expense.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Controlled Foreign-Related Transaction and Transfer Pricing Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List all cross-border transactions with related parties: sales, purchases, service fees, royalty payments, guarantees, interest, and intercompany reserve-asset transfers; state the transfer pricing method used and confirm whether the transaction is arm's length.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach or make available the Local File and Master File if the Korean entity's annual revenue is at least KRW 100 billion or cross-border related-party transactions exceed the statutory threshold from Law on Coordination of International Tax Affairs Article 11. Use approved methodologies; if TNMM is used, identify the tested party as the Korean EMI and provide interquartile benchmarking contemporaneously. NTS will automatically adjust and impose penalties for documentation that is prepared only after a tax audit notification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Withholding on Non-Resident Income and DTA Relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report dividends, interest, royalties, and other Korean-source income paid to non-residents during the tax year, the statutory withholding rate applied, any treaty-reduced rate claimed, and the amount remitted abroad.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Statutory combined withholding is 20% national plus 2% local surtax = 22% on outbound dividends, interest, and royalties. If a DTA reduction is claimed, attach the foreign shareholder's Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership declaration, form establishing treaty residence, and a statement that no Korean PE is attributable to the foreign payee. The treaty claim is not automatic; the payer must receive the TRC and Form 23 relief documentation before or at the time of remittance to apply the reduced rate at source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - Payment Summary, Credits, and Penalty Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile prepayments and interim payments, compute the remaining tax payment or refund, add any non-payment daily surcharges, and certify the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment of any remaining CIT is due with the return. If a non-resident withholding overpayment arises because a treaty was only documented after payment, the recipient must file a separate refund claim within the statutory period, not an adjustment to Box 9. Directors who knowingly sign a false summary face personal criminal exposure, and the NTS will block corporate dissolution until all tax, surcharge, and penalty amounts are paid.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a 20% unfiled-tax addition under Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-3(1), calculated on the unpaid tax; fraudulent or negligent under-reporting attracts up to 40% of the underpaid tax; failure to pay by the statutory due date accrues a daily non-payment surcharge on the unpaid national tax, plus the 10% local income tax on the CIT. Willful filing of false Korean-source income or false treaty claims is tax fraud under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment up to 2 years and a fine up to twice the evaded tax, with aggravated terms where the tax evaded exceeds statutory thresholds; a withholding agent who fails to withhold non-resident tax is liable for the unwithheld amount plus a 10% addition tax and may be prosecuted.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% combined statutory withholding on dividends paid by the Korean LLC to non-resident shareholders, comprising 20% national withholding under Corporate Tax Act Article 98(1) plus 2% local income tax surtax; bilateral tax treaties may reduce the combined rate to 5-10% on qualified dividends, typically subject to minimum shareholding and beneficial-ownership requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must: (i) obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate from the treaty jurisdiction and provide it to the Korean LLC as withholding agent; (ii) submit the NTS 'Application for Tax Treaty Reduction/Exemption of Non-Resident Income Tax' (Form 23-type), identifying the DTA article, the recipient's beneficial ownership, and the absence of a Korean permanent establishment; (iii) provide a beneficial ownership certificate with board resolution and financial substance evidence showing that the recipient has the right to use/control the income and is not a conduit; and (iv) notify the Korean payer in writing before remittance so the reduced treaty rate can be applied at source. If excess tax was withheld, the non-resident must file a refund claim with the NTS within the statutory time limit and provide the TRC retrospectively; no DTA relief is granted to a shell company lacking economic substance or to an intermediary that merely passes income to a resident of a third country.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory combined WHT on cross-border royalties and intercompany interest is 22% (20% national + 2% local surtax). Under Korean DTAs, interest and royalty rates are commonly reduced to 10-15% for beneficial owners, and certain interest may be exempt if paid to financial institutions/sovereign funds; royalties for the use of or right to use industrial, commercial, or scientific equipment, copyright, patent, trademark, know-how, and software require CUP documentation and must not be tainted by excessive charges or bundled service fees. Thin-capitalization interest disallowance applies before treaty relief, and the payer must demonstrate that the recipient is the true beneficial owner and has no Korean PE.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under the Law on Coordination of International Tax Affairs Article 11 and Enforcement Decree, mandatory Local File and Master File preparation applies when the Korean entity's annual revenue reaches KRW 100,000,000,000 or cross-border related-party transactions in a category exceed KRW 5,000,000,000 (with the CbC report threshold for an MNE group at consolidated revenue of KRW 1,500,000,000,000); documentation must be prepared contemporaneously and submitted to NTS within 30 days of request, with late or non-documentation penalties capped at prescribed amounts and additional adjustment penalties.
